title: Client Commitment Health Dossier and Contingency Catalog
content:
Purpose
This is a working dossier for use in upcoming QBRs and mid-cycle interventions. It consolidates high-signal indicators that track a customer’s likelihood to re-commit at next term, a ranked catalog of mitigation plays with recommended owners and timing windows, and a short escalations ladder for exec outreach if primary mitigations underperform.

Audience
Primary: CS lead assigned to the account (AM/CSM), Solutions Engineer, Renewal AE. Secondary: Head of Customer Success, VP Sales (for exec escalation), Product PM (for product-impact mitigations).

Executive snapshot (top line)
- Account: Meridian Analytics (faux client for template)
- Contract cadence: Annual renewal, $420k ARR, renewal in 90 days
- Current risk score (internal): 68/100 (Moderate-High)
- Immediate ask: Schedule 30-min exec alignment and allocate a product resource for short-term P0 bug fix (APM-9)

Key risk signals (ranked)
1) Usage slip: peak-consumption tokens down 42% vs. trailing 60d average.
2) Cost surprises: client reported higher-than-expected per-token billing; invoicing questions in support thread.
3) Feature gap: missing fine-grained routing for private deployment causes integration queue to pile up (ticket CS-8123).
4) Latency regressions: 95th percentile increased from 180ms to 420ms after last model swap.
5) Support sentiment: NPS-like thread in Slack shows rising negative tone (several messages flagged).

Signal scoring methodology (how we arrived at risk score)
- Each signal weighted by impact and immediacy (impact 1-5, immediacy 1-5).
- Example: Usage slip (impact 4, immediacy 5) = 20 points; Latency regression (impact 3, immediacy 4) = 12 points. Sum normalized to 0-100.
- Notes: This is intentionally aggressive — used to prioritize outbound intervention cadence.

Thresholds and actions (operational rules)
- Score 0-30: low touch. Auto-remediate via Optimize suggestions and product Q/A playbook.
- Score 31-60: medium touch. CS lead runs 1:1, schedule technical healthcall, enable cost guardrails.
- Score 61-85: high touch. Trigger contingency catalog plays (below), escalate to Solutions Engineering for two-week remediation sprint.
- Score 86-100: critical. Notify Head of CS and VP Sales; exec outreach + temporary credit/discount as a last resort.

Contingency catalog (mitigation plays)
- Play: Customer Cost Review (quick)
  - Purpose: align billing expectations, identify misconfigurations, apply temporary credits where justified.
  - Owner: Account Executive (renewal) + CS ops
  - Timebox: 72 hours
  - Success metric: invoice discrepancy resolved; client confirms billing forecast within 10%
  - Linked artifacts: JIRA CS-8119 (billing audit)

- Play: Latency Triage and Rollback
  - Purpose: investigate recent model swap regression, roll back to prior model variant if necessary.
  - Owner: SRE + Serving Runtime on-call
  - Timebox: 24-48 hours initial triage; rollback decision same window if SLA breached
  - Success metric: 95th percentile latency back within SLA (<=250ms)
  - Linked artifacts: internal runbook "latency-regression-first-response" (see Confluence link)

- Play: Product Patch Sprint (short-term)
  - Purpose: prioritize P0 integration issue causing fragmentation for private deploys
  - Owner: Product PM + Solutions Eng + Eng on call
  - Timebox: 2 weeks
  - Success metric: release hotfix; client integration validated in staging
  - Linked artifacts: GH PR 67, JIRA CS-8123

- Play: Executive Commitment Session (human touch)
  - Purpose: realign executive expectations, signal joint roadmap, surface commercial options
  - Owner: Head of CS + VP Sales
  - Timebox: schedule within 7 days
  - Success metric: execs agree on 90-day plan; obtain verbal commitment toward renewal

- Play: Short-term Concession (last-resort)
  - Purpose: apply limited credit or refresh contract terms to avoid churn while remediation happens
  - Owner: Sales Leader + Finance approval
  - Timebox: decision in 48 hours
  - Success metric: signed amendment or email confirmation of intent to renew

Escalation ladder (who to loop in and when)
- Tier 1: CSM + Solutions Eng — immediate after score crosses 60.
- Tier 2: CS Manager + Product PM — if not resolved within 5 business days or if new high-impact signal appears.
- Tier 3: Head of CS + VP Sales — if score stays >75 after two mitigation cycles or if contract value >$250k.
- Tier 4: CEO briefing — reserved for strategic accounts where retention risk threatens go-to-market commitments or large multi-year expansions.

QBR checklist (to include in slide pack)
- One-slide health summary: score, top 3 signals, next 90-day roadmap items that map to customer outcomes.
- Usage & cost charts: 30/60/90 day trendlines (tokens, sessions, peak latencies).
- Incident & ticket summary: top 5 open items with owners and ETA.
- Actions & asks: three prioritized asks for customer (e.g., enable feature flag, join weekly sync, approve test window).
- Commercial snapshot: renewal date, ARR, penalties/credits applied to date.

Meeting prep (CS lead)
- Pull last 90 days of usage (script: internal/analytics/query-usage.sql).
- Export billing run for last 2 invoices.
- Run cost-savings plan from Optimize module and attach recommendations.
- Confirm SE availability for live troubleshooting during QBR.
- Draft a one-paragraph executive summary for Head of CS review 48 hours before meeting.

Communication templates (shortcuts)
- Exec outreach subject: "Request: 30-min alignment on Meridian Analytics contract outlook"
- Body snippet (for Head of CS to send): "Quick ask: our team has identified a set of operational and product signals that materially affect your upcoming contract decision. We would like to schedule a 30-min alignment this week to review our proposed remediation plan and confirm next steps."

High-level transparency and guardrails
- Do not promise roadmap items beyond next 90 days during exec outreach. Use language: 'short-term mitigations + roadmap cadence.'
- Any commercial concession must be documented in SFDC and approved by Finance.

Open action items (working)
- [ ] CS-8123: confirm root cause steps for private deploy integration (owner: Maya Patel) — ETA 2026-03-05
- [ ] CS-8119: complete billing audit, communicate adjustments (owner: Diego Marquez) — ETA 2026-03-02
- [ ] Schedule Head of CS exec sync — owner: Alex Chen — target date 2026-03-04

Notes to self (working doc section)
- Consider adding a short-term 'safety throttle' we can toggle for heavy accounts to cap spend while keeping production paths active. Need Ops feasibility check.
- Evaluate if Optimize module can auto-generate a 1-page customer cost narrative for CS leads (low-effort internal feature).
- Follow up with Product on feasibility of per-customer routing policy (affects 3+ accounts currently flagged).

Revision log (top entries)
- 2025-11-02 Alexandra Chen: initial draft and scoring framework
- 2026-02-15 Sara Nguyen: added latency rollback runbook and updated playbook timeboxes
- 2026-02-28 Diego Marquez: inserted billing audit template and open action items

Unresolved questions
- What is the finance-approved maximum credit threshold for accounts under $500k ARR? (need policy link)
- Can we instrument an automated alert for billing anomalies at 20% deviation in the billing pipeline? (ask Data Platform)

Next steps (short)
- Finalize exec outreach draft and circulate to Head of CS by 2026-03-01.
- Kick billing audit and surface findings within 72 hours.
- Confirm SRE triage window and rollback authority for serving runtime.

References and templates
- Billing audit checklist (Confluence): CS/Billing/audit-checklist
- Latency triage runbook: infra/latency-regression-first-response
- Executive outreach email template: templates/exec-outreach-short.txt

— end of dossier (working)
